scene: You are at a baker's shop in the forum.
en: “Hello! What do you want?” “I want to buy bread.”
explain: _quid vīs?_ = what do you want? Answer with _volō_ + infinitive: _emere volō_ (I want to buy). The thing you buy is accusative: _pānem_.
distractors: The thing you buy is the object: accusative _pānem_.

en: “Do you have money?” “Yes, I have money.”
explain: _pecūniam_ is accusative singular: money is what you have.
distractors: What you have is the object: accusative _pecūniam_.
_minimē_ means “no”. The answer here is yes: _etiam_.

en: “I have bread. Do you want cheese?” “Yes, bread and cheese, please.”
explain: _quaesō_ = please. Both things you ask for are objects, so both are accusative: _pānem et cāseum_.
distractors: Both things are objects: accusative _cāseum_, not nominative _cāseus_.
Both things you ask for are objects: accusative _pānem_.

q: Dō tibi pānem et cāseum. Valē!
en: “I give you bread and cheese. Goodbye!” “Thank you, friend! Goodbye!”
explain: To speak to someone, Latin uses the vocative. For nouns in _-us_ it ends in _-e_: _amīcus_ becomes _amīce_.
distractors: Calling someone takes the vocative: _amīce_, not _amīcus_.
_amīcī_ is plural (“friends”). For one friend you call: _amīce_.

scene: You are lost in the city and a passer-by speaks to you.
en: “Hello! What are you looking for?” “I am looking for the forum.”
explain: _quaerō_ = I look for. The thing you look for is accusative; _forum_ looks the same in the nominative and the accusative (neuter nouns always do).
distractors: What you look for is the object: accusative _forum_, not ablative _forō_.

en: “The forum? It is near the baths.” “Where are the baths?”
explain: _thermae_ means “baths” and is always plural, so it takes _sunt_ (are), not _est_: _ubi sunt thermae?_
distractors: _quō?_ means “where to?”. To ask “where are they?” use _ubi_.

en: “The baths are in front of the temple. Do you understand?” “Yes, I understand. Thank you!”
explain: _intellegō_ = I understand. _etiam_ = yes. _grātiās tibi agō_ = thank you.

scene: A friend invites you to dinner.
q: Salvē! Hodiē cēnam parō. Venīsne ad cēnam?
en: “Hello! I am preparing dinner today. Will you come to dinner?” “Gladly! When do we dine?”
explain: _libenter_ = gladly. _quandō?_ asks “when?”. _cēnāmus_ is “we dine”: the ending _-mus_ is “we”.

en: “We dine at the ninth hour. What are you bringing?” “I am bringing wine and apples.”
explain: _portō_ = I carry, I bring. Both things are objects: _vīnum_ (accusative singular) and _pōma_ (accusative plural).
distractors: What you bring is the object: accusative _vīnum_, not ablative _vīnō_.
